I am 45 this year, and I have farmed here in Quzhou for 20 years, so I mostly go by what I have seen on my own land and what the better farmers around me are doing. I only finished middle school, so I do pay attention to fertilizer rate and timing, but I do not calculate too finely. This year I will keep the land spread out, not put everything into one crop. Cotton and stevia give cash, but they also tie up labor and money. Wheat and maize are steadier, and with my well I can protect them if the rain is poor. On the wheat-maize land I will stay close to the usual local practice, because changing too much is risky. On cotton and stevia I will control the area and inputs so I do not squeeze the household cash too hard at the start of the season.

For the 58.1 mu, I will arrange it like this: 20 mu in winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 20 mu, 18.1 mu in cotton, and 20 mu in stevia. Wheat and maize are my stable grain income, cotton is still worth planting on some land because I know how to manage it, and stevia can make money if the stand is good, but I will not expand it further because it needs careful management. For wheat I will use a normal base fertilizer and one topdress at jointing, with about 3 irrigations if the season is normal. For maize after wheat harvest, the turnaround is tight, so I will use rotary tillage and quick sowing, put most fertilizer near planting, and irrigate only if the rains do not come. Cotton and stevia I will watch more field by field, especially weeds and insects, because if I miss the timing there, the loss is bigger.

I keep 20 mu in wheat-maize because that is the most reliable here, and my well gives me some protection in a dry spell. Cotton and stevia can bring cash, but they need more watching, more labor, and more money at the front end, so I do not want to over-expand them.
